Goals for Budget Period 3 included testing with MEA, ICE-21™, and ICE-31®, data analysis, and final reporting. 3.2 Scope of Work 3.2.1 Budget Period 1 - Design Phase In this phase, ION designed the 10 tpd CO capture system and the BOP systems needed to 2 support the 1 MWe engineering scale capture system at the NGCC facility. Additionally, during this phase of the project, a HAZOP study was conducted for the engineering scale system, which helped shape the detailed design. The phase concluded with design packages, a fixed price cost to be compared against the budget, and an executed Host Site Agreement. 3.2.2 Budget Period 2 - Construction Phase This phase encompassed the procurement of necessary equipment and materials for both the BOP and CO capture systems. Upon receipt of the above, the BOP and CO capture systems were 2 2 fabricated according to approved designs. The control software was developed and made ready for Factory Acceptance Testing once the construction activities were completed. ION also completed ION Clean Energy 6 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT solvent procurement and Test Plan preparation. This phase concluded with the transportation of the CO capture system to the host site, the fabrication of the necessary BOP tie-ins, and the Site 2 Acceptance Testing (SAT) to verify operations. 3.2.3 Budget Period 3 - Testing Phase This phase commenced with the final shakedown testing of the engineering-scale system, followed by baselining the system against the 1st generation MEA solvent. ION then ran its 2nd generation solvent (ICE-21™) on the engineering scale system for baseline results of an advanced solvent before switching to ICE-31®. Once the ICE-31® solvent was in the system, the test plan involved the same baseline parametric testing performed on the previous solvents for a direct comparison, before moving on to a long-term testing strategy to evaluate the solvent lifetime under continuous cycling of operations required to follow the NGCC system. The purpose of this long- term testing was to evaluate the solvent performance for a long enough duration to fully understand the interactions and degradation pathways of the solvent and flue gas. ION maintained the solvent and byproduct concentration through solvent analysis, solvent dosing, and continuous slipstream reclaiming throughout the test campaign to ensure consistent performance and to determine an accurate makeup rate for the solvent.
